newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki up but lost early steam, eyes on Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki up but lost early steam, eyes on Wall St.

text.p: Shares ended up but drifted clearly off highs in late trade on Tuesday as U.S. stocks opened mixed, and the overall market ended just a whisker off its lows as eyes again turned to Wall Street for direction, brokers said.
The HEX general index closed up 0.51 percent at 2,834.30 points -- trading in a 2,836.00-2,856.91 range -- and the FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark rose 0.50 percent to 987.14.

Telecoms group Nokia led the market to a strong early session after gains in the U.S. ahead of rival Motorola's Q1 report. It hit 310.00 markka but closed at 305.00 markka, up three. Its U.S. close corresponded to 304.95 markka.
Motorola's report came late on Monday and Wall Street's full reaction was expected on Tuesday. Motorola traded $0-7/8 lower at $59-3/8 in the morning in New York.
Overall, brokers said the day's rise looked fragile and would depend entirely on how the U.S. stock market fared: "This was a rather lax day, with hardly anybody daring to do anything," said one.
Nokia accounted for 32 percent of moderate at 550 million markka volume.
The dollar's strength -- at the Helsinki treasury market close USD/FIM was 5.1065 compared to 5.0975 on Monday -- also supported Nokia and cyclicals, brokers said.
Sampo and Konecranes both rose on big block trades.
Cranemaker Konecranes rose 6.00 markka or 3.16 percent to 196.00 and insurer Sampo was up 4.00 at 457.00 in 46 million markka volume.
